new_claims.claim: A nonconstant Boolean membership oracle is an exact standard-HSP oracle for its translation stabilizer iff that stabilizer has index 2 and the marked set is one coset.
For an H-invariant Boolean subset of F_2^n, Walsh-Fourier support lies in H-perp.
If the exact stabilizer H is known, exhaustive membership search factors through G/H and gains an exact |H|-fold state reduction.
On the finite n=10 audit, genuine coupled XOR symmetries were common in XOR systems, present in some 2-SAT, and rare in the tested 3-SAT panels.
The Boolean SAT indicator failed the ordinary HSP promise on every tested 2-SAT and 3-SAT instance; higher-rank XOR systems also generally failed it despite exact symmetry.
Walsh spectral concentration did not provide a stable monotone predictor of deterministic 3-SAT enumeration cost across the tested clause-density panels.

next_necessity.observation: Shor/Simon-style periodicity is highly effective only when the search oracle exposes an appropriate coset structure. Generic SAT membership usually does not.
next_necessity.action: Use Fourier/HSP as a structure detector and quotient carrier only after exact or certified symmetry is found.
next_necessity.necessity: For generic NP search, find a richer efficiently discoverable partition/representation or return to Partial-Hard/Range-Avoidance rather than assume a hidden period.
